---
title: Employee schema qualification
description: Qualify the employee creation and restoration schema in an exact-source disposable database.
---

Run `employee-schema-contract.yaml` from a reviewed control revision and set
`source_sha` to the full reviewed creation/restoration stack commit. The workflow
keeps the trusted control checkout at the workspace root for the shared setup
action and checks out the exact source under `source/`. Commands run from that
source directory invoke the reviewed control scripts via `../apps` and
`../scripts`; they never substitute current main or
connect to staging or production. Its installed CLI starts a disposable
full-migration Supabase project using the same isolated runner as the Tutoring
contract gates. Startup/reset and each fixture are bounded; an always-run cleanup
step stops only the owned project, without retaining a database backup.

The foundation gate requires all five packets: signup guards (25), administrator
(20), finalization (34), identity contract (52), and restoration (41). Each packet
must emit one complete, sequential, non-skipped pgTAP plan and close its synthetic
transaction with rollback. Missing packets, a different count, failed SQL,
truncated output, or unsuccessful cleanup fail the gate. The private command
output is not uploaded; the small JSON artifact binds the exact source and fixture
hashes to the 172 assertions and cleanup outcome.

Verify the helper with
`node --test apps/database/scripts/employee-schema-tap.test.mjs`.
A green schema result is not native admission/lease/fence qualification, a GoTrue
or provider transaction, employee activation, or production SQL application.
The feedback layer's 105 assertions remain a separate later stack qualification;
they are not silently included or waived by this foundation job.

If the schema runner fails after its private receipt directory exists, the receipt
includes a fixed `failureDiagnostic`: the first failing phase, packet ordinal,
bounded exit status, timeout/signal indicators, and TAP failure flags/counts. It
contains no assertion descriptions, SQL, exception messages, container paths, or
credentials. A diagnostic is evidence about the failed stage, not a passing
packet; verify the same exact source and keep all failed attempts.

The bounded failure diagnostic also records numeric `failedAssertionOrdinals`
only when the TAP numbers are unique, increasing, within the frozen packet's
assertion range, and agree with the failure count. Malformed or oversized evidence
sets `assertionOrdinalsValid` to false and emits an empty array. Match valid numbers
to the exact frozen fixture offline; descriptions and expected/actual values are
never exposed. These numbers locate failures and do not change any passing gate.

### Signup exception contract diagnostics

For failed first-packet assertions 22 and 23 only, the receipt can include the
actual five-character SQLSTATE and a boolean comparison against the fixed expected
message. Caught messages, wanted messages, SQL, identities and TAP descriptions
remain private. Unknown or inconsistent pgTAP diagnostic formats emit invalid
classification with null values; absence of an exception is not inferred. These
diagnostics do not alter the expected 23514 contracts or the strict 172-assertion
success and cleanup gates. The previous timing-only fixture change remained
unqualified after both assertions failed again.

Validated caught records also include a fixed message category for the four
owned creation-denial literals: intent missing, pending required, identity tuple
mismatch, or registry missing. Any other message becomes `other_redacted`.
Unknown or inconsistent diagnostic formats keep the category null. Matching is
exact: whitespace, case, continuation lines and runtime values are never
normalized into an owned category. These enums identify evidence; they do not
change fixture expectations, security checks or schema qualification.

A separate `constraintCategory` classifies six exact generated CHECK-message
relation/constraint pairs from the frozen creation migration: creation-intent
staff email/name and employee staff email/name/lifecycle/recovery. The original
`messageCategory` remains `other_redacted`. Generated messages omit schema, so
schema identity is not inferred. SQLSTATE must be 23514; unknown pairs or altered
text remain `other_redacted`; invalid caught evidence emits null. This diagnostic
does not change SQL, the 25 assertions or the strict 172-assertion success gate.

## Composed source and public consumer qualification

The workflow's `qualification` choice selects `foundation` or `composed`.
Foundation retains the original five rollback packets and 172 assertions.
Composed selects `employee-creation-composed-reviewed-auth-declaration-v1`,
preserving those packets and adding the operation journal and reserved preflight
packets for 281 assertions.
The additional source checks do not authorize employee creation or production.

The current default requires source
`f8696ed991cfa4b6c51bb86d59a93632cb5da2af`, tree
`df8329077114ab799dd2f4b0a8d30c773574f6a5`, and sole parent
`9224768b9789c525e05b78f9e381949f91267a8f`. Its nested reviewed marker recipe
binds that parent to `794789f41e26d01e9029a3ff92bbbf4f1e738b25`. Actual commit
headers, trees, source blobs and the exact six-file auth declaration parent delta
must match the closed reviewed recipe.

Both control and source checkouts retain full history with `fetch-depth: 0`.
The source checkout still uses the exact `inputs.source_sha` under `source/`,
with persisted credentials disabled. Reachable objects provide the pinned
f869-to-922-to-794 chain. Missing commit, tree or blob objects, incorrect ancestry
or an unlisted source change fail closed before runtime; history depth does not
change exact source or control admission.

Root must supply the exact committed full-union source S through both
`source_sha` and `authoritative_source_sha`. The controller verifies the actual
checkout HEAD and clean tracked source. Missing or mismatched S, the historical
foundation source, and the inherited consumer-only commit are denied before
network creation. Source approval and a commit-shaped string do not establish
qualification. The control checkout is independently hashed against its exact
control commit C before runtime admission.

The import-safe qualification adapter hashes observed file bytes. The raw ordered forty-file
V1 profile permits exactly two reviewed changes: the SQL marker hash
39c56-to-d78c and `bun.lock` 2c1db-to-8a1cd. Every other row, the five migrations
and seven packet hashes retain their exact original identities. Immutable V1
continues to reject the amended rows; the successor validates its own recipe
without rewriting observations or substituting rows for V1.

The original 47-row closure contains those forty source rows, two immutable
profile modules and the independent five-file public consumer closure. The
six-file auth declaration recipe (`auth6`) adds the root package, lock, declaration
patch, two private type controls and operating docs. Deduplicating the lock
overlap yields 52 unique observed paths. The full source/dependency digest and
separate consumer and control digests bind every subsequent composed receipt.
These raw recipe bytes establish source identity; installed runtime bytes require
separate evidence. Missing, changed, duplicated or reordered source, migration, packet,
control or consumer entries fail closed. The seven actual command results must
have exit code zero, complete strict TAP plans, no SKIP or TODO, and full
BEGIN/ROLLBACK closure. Synthetic TAP validates transcripts only and leaves all
qualification flags false.

Composed qualification reads actual `pg_get_functiondef` definitions and the
applied migration ledger from the same owned database before generating types.
It rechecks the catalog after type generation and after consumer compilation.
Definition hashes are hashes of current PostgreSQL catalog bytes, never hashes
of migration source. Catalog, generated types and strict public consumer
receipts bind the same source, control, project, schema snapshot, network,
full-source digest and consumer closure. Catalog drift or identity mismatch
denies qualification.

The consumer compiler uses a disposable source view with actual source files
and the real generated artifact at the canonical
`packages/types/src/supabase.ts` location. It checks the actual public
`@tuturuuu/internal-api/infrastructure` entry, legacy and journaled call
identities, the boundary, journal, store, phase adapter, supplier and fixed SQL
consumers. Inventory SQL subpaths resolve from the actual package exports.
Strict, no-emit compilation keeps `skipLibCheck` false and
`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` true. There are no invented RPC declarations,
private employee aliases or copied declarations. Compiler errors remain a
consumer qualification failure; transfer the failing source path to its owner
instead of widening the controller reservation.

The controller requires the complete packet, catalog, generated-type and real
compiler receipt chain, successful lifecycle and owned database cleanup, and
existing network, relay and worker-drain guards. Missing receipts, compiler
failure, failed cleanup or changed artifact bytes keep composed schema, type,
catalog and consumer admission false. Combined qualification still requires the
existing independently verified network cleanup. TLS, fixed-worker COMMIT,
races, provider, account and production admission remain separate pending gates.
Focused adapter and consumer tests cover the denial boundaries with synthetic
parser controls and observed source bytes; they do not execute SQL or qualify a
runtime.

The exact-source validator separately selects
`employee-creation-composed-reviewed-marker-v1` for the exact reviewed 922 source.
That selection is a source validator contract; hosted execution uses the current
auth declaration default. The nested marker recipe retains its original SQL
amendment and five provenance digests. The auth successor additionally pins its
six-file freeze, independent review, committed checkpoint and full source/auth
manifest. Descendants, generic overrides and changed provenance are denied.

The retained strict static compile receipt
`420a52e942af1cf4fc6897a238b3378b2d085a776055498a5227013853997363`
records a passing source/dependency recipe unit. It does not establish generated
same-applied schema types, SQL execution, runtime library bytes or account/Auth
behavior. Composed schema, types, catalog, consumer, runtime, account, Auth,
provider and production qualification flags remain false without the complete
real same-applied source/control/project/snapshot/network receipt chain and
separately admitted runtime evidence. Source authorization and synthetic parser
success remain separate from those receipts.

## Bounded network failure diagnostics

The existing network predicates and their `qualified` conjunction are unchanged.
A pure helper adds a closed nine-predicate vector with `PASS`, `FAIL` and
`UNKNOWN`, plus bounded deduplicated reason counts and at most one integer
ordinal witness per category. Unobserved event, start, destroy or stream outcomes
remain unknown. A complete retained create-image set can establish missing
postgres-meta evidence; it cannot reconstruct the other predicates or explain
why that image is missing.

Diagnostics use the already selected in-memory live/history events and existing
subscription, marker, history and drain results. There are no additional Docker
reads or subscriptions. Byte, event, pending-line, deadline and group-drain caps,
exclusive network ownership and ordinary cleanup guards remain intact. The
collector admits only the strict bounded vector shape, preserving the original
qualification and drain booleans. Malformed vectors are denied while later
independent finalizers still run. Diagnostic fields contain no raw Docker labels,
foreign IDs, names, image strings, environment values, SQL, stderr or exceptions.
The existing exact source/control/run/attempt/network/nonce qualification receipt
is capped at 64 KiB before it is written. A passing vector never upgrades a
failed qualification boolean.

The controller writes a version 1 qualification envelope for both validated and
denied packet outcomes. Network cleanup still requires exact attempt ownership
and every worker drain receipt; schema qualification is not required to clean up
a safely drained failed attempt.

After strict consumer compilation, the controller reobserves the complete
selected source closure, including supplier and journal files outside the five
public consumer rows. Any identity, row, byte hash or digest change denies
admission inside the lifecycle cleanup boundary. Generated artifact and applied
catalog checks remain separate requirements.
